title: Angle Relationships
seo_title: Grade 7 Angle Relationships Worksheets: Complementary, Supplementary, Vertical and Adjacent Angles
standard_text: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 angle relationships worksheets: complementary, supplementary, vertical and adjacent angles, angles on a line and around a point, and equations for unknown angles. 100 practice questions with diagrams and an answer key.
key_big: Complementary angles add to 90°. Supplementary angles add to 180°. Vertical angles are equal.
key_sub: Angles on a straight line add to 180° and angles around a point add to 360°. Write an equation, then solve it.
body_html:
Angle pairs

Many angle problems use just three facts: a right angle is 90°, a straight line is 180°, and a full turn is 360°.

NameRuleExample
Complementaryadd to 90°35° and 55°
Supplementaryadd to 180° (a straight line)60° and 120°
Verticalacross from each other, equal50° and 50°
Around a pointadd to 360°100° + 120° + 140°
Example

Angles of (2x + 10)° and 50° are supplementary. Find x.

Write an equation: 2x + 10 + 50 = 180.

Combine: 2x + 60 = 180, so 2x = 120.

Divide: x = 60.

Answer: x = 60

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the totals: complementary is 90°, supplementary is 180°.
  • Adding vertical angles to 180°: vertical angles are equal. The angles next to each other add to 180°.
  • Stopping at x: if the question asks for the angle, put x back into the expression.

faq.q: What is the difference between complementary and supplementary angles?
faq.a: Complementary angles add to 90°, like 30° and 60°. Supplementary angles add to 180°, like 30° and 150°.
When two lines cross, the angles across from each other are vertical angles. They are always equal.
Angles that share a vertex and one side without overlapping. Two adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary.

faq.q: How do I find an unknown angle with x?
faq.a: Use the angle fact to write an equation, such as (2x + 10) + 50 = 180. Solve for x, then put x back in if the question asks for the angle.

items.q: What is the complement of a 35° angle?
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°: 90 − 35 = 55. Not 145°: that is the supplement (180°).

items.q: What is the complement of a 62° angle?
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°: 90 − 62 = 28. Not 118°: that is the supplement (180°).

items.q: What is the complement of a 18° angle?
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°: 90 − 18 = 72. Not 162°: that is the supplement (180°).

items.q: What is the complement of a 81° angle?
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°: 90 − 81 = 9. Not 99°: that is the supplement (180°).

items.q: What is the complement of a 47° angle?
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°: 90 − 47 = 43. Not 133°: that is the supplement (180°).

items.q: What is the complement of a 74° angle?
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°: 90 − 74 = 16. Not 106°: that is the supplement (180°).

items.q: What is the supplement of a 70° angle?
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°: 180 − 70 = 110. Not 20°: that is the complement (90°).

items.q: What is the supplement of a 125° angle?
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°: 180 − 125 = 55.

items.q: What is the supplement of a 33° angle?
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°: 180 − 33 = 147. Not 57°: that is the complement (90°).

items.q: What is the supplement of a 148° angle?
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°: 180 − 148 = 32.

items.q: What is the supplement of a 96° angle?
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°: 180 − 96 = 84.

items.q: What is the supplement of a 15° angle?
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°: 180 − 15 = 165. Not 75°: that is the complement (90°).

items.q: Two angles that add to 90° are called ____.
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°. Tip: C comes before S, and 90 comes before 180.

items.q: Two angles that add to 180° are called ____.
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°, like the two angles on a straight line.

items.q: When two lines cross, the angles opposite each other are called ____.
items.e: Vertical angles are across from each other where two lines cross. They are equal.

items.q: Two angles that share a vertex and a side, but do not overlap, are called ____.
items.e: Adjacent means next to each other: same vertex, one shared side, no overlap.

items.q: Vertical angles are always ____.
items.e: Vertical angles are always equal (congruent). They add to 180° only if both are 90°.

items.q: Can two angles of 40° and 50° be complementary?
items.e: 40 + 50 = 90, so they are complementary. Complementary angles do not have to be next to each other.

items.q: Which pair of angles is supplementary?
An angle is equal to its complement. How big is it?

items.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 60°. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The vertical angle is also 60°. The two angles next to it are 180 − 60 = 120° each.

items.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 145°. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The vertical angle is also 145°. The two angles next to it are 180 − 145 = 35° each.

items.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 48°. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The vertical angle is also 48°. The two angles next to it are 180 − 48 = 132° each.

items.q: Two lines cross and one angle is 90°. What are the other angles?
items.e: The vertical angle is 90°, and the angles next to it are 180 − 90 = 90°. The lines are perpendicular.

items.q: Two lines cross. The sum of two vertical angles is 100°. How big is each of them?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal, so each is 100 ÷ 2 = 50°.

items.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 3 times as big as the angle next to it. What is the smaller angle?
items.e: The two angles are supplementary: x + 3x = 180, so 4x = 180 and x = 45°.

items.q: Angles of x° and 50° are complementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are complementary, so x + 50 = 90. Subtract 50: x = 40.

items.q: Angles of 2x° and 40° are supplementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are supplementary, so 2x + 40 = 180. Subtract 40: 2x = 140. Divide by 2: x = 70. Not 140: that is the size of the angle, not x.

items.q: Angles of (x + 15)° and 35° are complementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are complementary, so (x + 15) + 35 = 90. Subtract 50: x = 40. Not 55: that is the size of the angle, not x.

items.q: Angles of 3x° and 60° are supplementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are supplementary, so 3x + 60 = 180. Subtract 60: 3x = 120. Divide by 3: x = 40. Not 120: that is the size of the angle, not x.

items.q: Angles of (2x + 10)° and 50° are complementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are complementary, so (2x + 10) + 50 = 90. Subtract 60: 2x = 30. Divide by 2: x = 15. Not 40: that is the size of the angle, not x.

items.q: Angles of (4x + 20)° and 40° are supplementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are supplementary, so (4x + 20) + 40 = 180. Subtract 60: 4x = 120. Divide by 4: x = 30. Not 140: that is the size of the angle, not x.

items.q: Angles of (5x − 10)° and 40° are supplementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are supplementary, so (5x − 10) + 40 = 180. Subtract 30: 5x = 150. Divide by 5: x = 30. Not 140: that is the size of the angle, not x.

items.q: Angles of (3x + 6)° and 24° are complementary. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are complementary, so (3x + 6) + 24 = 90. Subtract 30: 3x = 60. Divide by 3: x = 20. Not 66: that is the size of the angle, not x.

items.q: Angles of (x + 20)° and (x + 40)° are supplementary. What is x?
items.e: x + 20 + x + 40 = 180. Combine like terms: 2x + 60 = 180, so 2x = 120 and x = 60. The angles are 80° and 100°.

items.q: Angles of 2x° and 3x° are complementary. What is x?
items.e: 2x + 3x = 90. Combine like terms: 5x = 90, so x = 18. The angles are 36° and 54°.

items.q: Angles of (3x + 10)° and (2x + 20)° are supplementary. What is x?
items.e: 3x + 10 + 2x + 20 = 180. Combine like terms: 5x + 30 = 180, so 5x = 150 and x = 30. The angles are 100° and 80°.

items.q: Angles of x° and (4x + 10)° are complementary. What is x?
items.e: x + 4x + 10 = 90. Combine like terms: 5x + 10 = 90, so 5x = 80 and x = 16. The angles are 16° and 74°.

items.q: Angles of 5x° and x° are supplementary. What is x?
items.e: 5x + x = 180. Combine like terms: 6x = 180, so x = 30. The angles are 150° and 30°.

items.q: Angles of (2x + 5)° and (x + 25)° are complementary. What is x?
items.e: 2x + 5 + x + 25 = 90. Combine like terms: 3x + 30 = 90, so 3x = 60 and x = 20. The angles are 45° and 45°.

items.q: Two lines cross. Vertical angles measure (2x + 10)° and (x + 40)°. How big is each angle?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal: 2x + 10 = x + 40, so x = 30. Each angle is 2(30) + 10 = 70°.

items.q: Two lines cross. Vertical angles measure (3x)° and (x + 50)°. How big is each angle?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal: 3x = x + 50, so x = 25. Each angle is 3(25) = 75°.

items.q: Two lines cross. Vertical angles measure (4x − 20)° and (2x + 30)°. How big is each angle?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal: 4x − 20 = 2x + 30, so x = 25. Each angle is 4(25) − 20 = 80°.

items.q: Two lines cross. Vertical angles measure (5x + 10)° and (3x + 30)°. How big is each angle?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal: 5x + 10 = 3x + 30, so x = 10. Each angle is 5(10) + 10 = 60°.

items.q: Two lines cross. Vertical angles measure (3x + 15)° and (x + 55)°. How big is each angle?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal: 3x + 15 = x + 55, so x = 20. Each angle is 3(20) + 15 = 75°.

items.q: Two lines cross. Vertical angles measure (6x)° and (4x + 24)°. How big is each angle?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal: 6x = 4x + 24, so x = 12. Each angle is 6(12) = 72°.

items.q: A ladder leans against a wall. It makes a 68° angle with the ground. What angle does it make with the wall? (The wall meets the ground at 90°.)
items.e: The ground, wall and ladder make a triangle with a right angle. The two other angles are complementary: 90 − 68 = 22°.

items.q: A road crosses a railway track. One angle between them is 57°. What is the angle next to it on the same side of the track?
items.e: The two angles are on a straight line: 180 − 57 = 123°.

items.q: A pizza is cut into slices from the centre. Three slices have angles 70°, 85° and 95°. The rest is one slice. What is its angle?
items.e: Angles around the centre add to 360°: 360 − (70 + 85 + 95) = 360 − 250 = 110°.

items.q: The hands of a clock at 3:00 make a right angle. A second hand splits it into two angles. One is 34°. What is the other?
items.e: The two angles make 90°: 90 − 34 = 56°.

items.q: Two angles are supplementary. One is 4 times the other. What is the larger angle?
items.e: x + 4x = 180, so 5x = 180 and x = 36. The larger angle is 4 × 36 = 144°. Not 36°: that is the smaller angle.

items.q: Two angles are complementary. One is 20° more than the other. What is the smaller angle?
items.e: x + (x + 20) = 90, so 2x = 70 and x = 35°. The other is 55°.

items.q: Two angles are supplementary. One is 30° less than twice the other. What is the smaller angle?
A door is opened so it makes a 115° angle with the wall on one side. What angle does it make with the wall on the other side?
items.e: The wall is a straight line, so the two angles add to 180°: 180 − 115 = 65°.

items.q: A kite string makes a 38° angle with the ground. What is the angle between the string and a pole standing straight up from the same point?
items.e: The pole and the ground make 90°. 90 − 38 = 52°.

items.q: A fan has 5 blades spaced evenly around the centre. What is the angle between two blades next to each other?
items.e: The blades split 360° into 5 equal parts: 360 ÷ 5 = 72°. Not 36°: that splits 180°.

items.q: Three rays split a straight line into angles of x°, 2x° and 3x°. What is the largest angle?
items.e: x + 2x + 3x = 180, so 6x = 180 and x = 30. The largest is 3 × 30 = 90°.

items.q: The angles around a point are x°, x°, 100° and 120°. What is x?
An angle's supplement is 3 times its complement. How big is the angle?
A ramp makes a 12° angle with the flat ground. What is the angle between the ramp and the ground on the other side of the ramp's bottom edge?
items.e: The ground is a straight line, so 180 − 12 = 168°.

items.q: Two streets cross. One corner has an angle of (2x + 30)°. The corner across from it is (4x − 10)°. How big is that corner angle?
items.e: Vertical angles are equal: 2x + 30 = 4x − 10, so 40 = 2x and x = 20. The angle is 2(20) + 30 = 70°. Not 20: that is x.

items.q: An angle is 40° more than its supplement. How big is the angle?
items.e: x + (x − 40) = 180, so 2x = 220 and x = 110°. Its supplement is 70°.

items.q: A beam of light hits a flat mirror. It comes in at 35° to the mirror and leaves at 35° on the other side. What is the angle between the two beams?
items.e: The three angles are on the straight mirror: 35 + ? + 35 = 180, so ? = 110°.

items.q: A wheel has 8 spokes evenly spaced. What is the angle between two spokes next to each other?
A ceiling fan blade turns from pointing north to pointing east. Then it turns 30° more. How far has it turned in all?
items.e: North to east is a quarter turn, 90°. 90 + 30 = 120°.
